hits.text: 18 March – Charles H. Bennett and Gilles Brassard are awarded the 2025 Turing Award for their work in quantum information science.
Japanese researcher Tokuji Unno wins the Ig Nobel Prize for his 1977 paper “How to Blow the Nose — An Aerodynamic Study of the Nose Blowing.”
2025 | | Charles H. Bennett | "For their essential role in igniting and shaping the quantum revolution in computer science and in information and communications technology." | IBM Research

The first recipient, in 1966, was Alan Perlis. The youngest recipient was Donald Knuth, who won in 1974 at the age of 36, while the oldest recipient was Alfred Aho, who won in 2020 at the age of 79. Three women have been awarded the prize: Frances Allen (in 2006), Barbara Liskov (in 2008), and Shafi Goldwasser (in 2012).
